W2 (empirical), after E033. Tip is E033: 5.691 s, 0.7536 on seeds 0-2 (20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30%, 8.75 epochs, 219 steps, batch 2000, wd x0.5). Held-out is about 0.7526 on the E027 base, so the real margin over the 0.753 bar is about zero.

Mechanisms, each tied to measured runs:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0.0-0.2 pp (E020, E023, E027). The tip sits at the accuracy floor.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, E006, confounded) are in the tip. The Lookahead settings look tuned. A harder pull (E025), a longer interval (E030) and late LS=0 (E032) all hurt by 0.3-0.7 pp. Time-neutral boosters have failed 5 times in a row. wd, LS, Muon lr, LR floor and warm-up were flat within noise (E013, E014, E022, E029).
3. Time tracks pixels and FLOPs, sublinearly on small maps. Early low-res is nearly free (E026, E033: -0.19 s for -0.01 pp on seeds 0-2). The 28 px and 32 px phases carry the accuracy (E018, E024).
4. Skipping backward work (E028 freeze: -0.5 s, -0.35 pp on seeds 0-2) and selecting examples (E031) trade at about 0.3-0.5 pp per 0.5 s. That is a worse rate than the epoch dial.
5. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any change to step count or RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. Held-out sits about 0.2 pp below seeds 0-2. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: I overpredicted time on trims (savings run 2-8% larger than modelled), and I was too optimistic on time-neutral accuracy changes.

Unsure: whether the freeze plus extra epochs nets positive. The freeze saves about 0.5 s and costs about 0.35 pp. Adding 0.5 epoch costs about 0.3 s and returns maybe 0.1-0.2 pp, so the stack probably sits below the bar. Also unsure whether the prepare cleanup (H3.2.1) is worth more than 0.05-0.1 s. It is bit-identical if the op order holds, so accuracy is unchanged and the time saving is small but safe.

forecasts.reason: Freeze saves about 0.5 s, 0.5 epoch adds about 0.3 s, and net accuracy is likely just under 0.753.
A bit-identical change keeps accuracy unchanged and saves about 0.05 s from trial 0.
It likely saves 2-4% but shifts the RNG, and the accuracy loss is about 0.1-0.2 pp.
A longer freeze saves more time but loses more accuracy, at the worse rate E028 showed.
It is a diagnostic. The fresh-seed mean is likely about 0.7525, near the bar.
It adds a few percent of savings on top of the freeze, but the added complexity risks accuracy drift.
A profiling run with no recipe change leaves the metrics identical. Non-GEMM kernels probably take 30% or more of GPU time.
Dropping Muon saves about 3% of time and probably loses 0.2-0.5 pp.

cruxes: Is the tip's true population mean (fresh seeds) at or above 0.753? If it is below, every further time cut needs an accuracy gain first.
Does the freeze (E028) plus 0.5 epoch net out positive on held-out seeds? That depends on whether the freeze costs 0.35 pp or only the 0.1-0.2 pp that noise would allow.
How much of the remaining 5.69 s is fixed overhead (prepare, trial-0 warm-up, Muon/Lookahead launches) as opposed to pixel-proportional compute?
